articles.title: Russia Hacked Routers to Steal Microsoft Office Tokens
articles.summary: Microsoft just dropped 167 security fixes including a SharePoint zero-day and a Windows Defender flaw called 'BlueHammer' — because apparently even the security software needs securing. Chrome also patched its fourth zero-day this year, keeping the vulnerability Olympics competitive.

articles.title: OpenAI locks GPT-5.5-Cyber behind velvet rope despite slamming Anthropic for doing exactly that
articles.summary: Critical cPanel vulnerability is already being exploited in the wild with ransomware following close behind, because hosting millions of websites with unpatched flaws is apparently someone's idea of fun. CISA fast-tracked this to their 'oh shit' list for good reason.

articles.title: Trellix Confirms Source Code Breach With Unauthorized Repository Access
articles.summary: CISA added CVE-2026-31431 to their Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog — a Linux root access bug that's being actively hammered in the wild. When the government's cyber watchdogs are screaming 'patch now,' you should probably listen.

articles.title: CVE-2026-31431: Copy Fail vulnerability enables Linux root privilege escalation across cloud environments
articles.summary: A 15-year-old script kiddie allegedly breached France's national ID agency and tried to sell millions of citizens' data on the dark web. The future of cybercrime is apparently old enough to need parental permission for a bank account but young enough to pwn a nation.

articles.title: 30,000 Facebook Accounts Hacked via Google AppSheet Phishing Campaign
articles.summary: Trellix, a cybersecurity company whose entire job is preventing breaches, just admitted hackers accessed their source code repository. The irony is so thick you could cut it with a butter knife dipped in privilege escalation exploits.

articles.title: Digital Hopes, Real Power: From Connection to Collective Action
articles.summary: Public records laws exposed how law enforcement's automated license plate readers create sprawling surveillance networks — so naturally, states are now trying to hide this data from the public. Democracy dies in darkness, but surveillance thrives there.

articles.title: Open Records Laws Reveal ALPRs’ Sprawling Surveillance. Now States Want to Block What the Public Sees.
articles.summary: Utah's new anti-VPN law goes into effect next week, because nothing says 'land of the free' like legislating away digital privacy tools. Expect VPN usage to surge faster than lawmakers can spell 'First Amendment.'

articles.title: Patch Tuesday, April 2026 Edition
articles.summary: Tyler 'Tylerb' Buchanan, a senior Scattered Spider member, pleaded guilty to wire fraud and identity theft after their SMS phishing campaigns. Another one bites the dust in the eternal cat-and-mouse game of cybercrime justice.

articles.title: A Bridge to Somewhere: How to Link Your Mastodon, Bluesky, or Other Federated Accounts
articles.summary: Germany just doxxed 'UNKN,' the mastermind behind REvil and GandCrab ransomware gangs — turns out 31-year-old Daniil Shchukin was running the show behind 130+ acts of digital mayhem. The hunter becomes the hunted, with proper attribution and everything.

articles.title: First reports come in of victims of critical cPanel vuln as 'millions' of sites potentially exposed
articles.summary: Britain's cyber agency warns that AI-powered bug hunting is about to unleash decades of buried code flaws all at once — like archaeological excavation, but for vulnerabilities. The technical debt chickens are coming home to roost, and they're armed with CVE numbers.
